answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price identity itself. Before an agent may whisper into the ledger, it must burn a non-refundable entry fee, making the network a costly haven rather than free pasture. The nectar of mining rewards flows only to agents whose peers vouch across many epochs, so one honest identity earns steady yield while an attacker farming thousands of fake ones pays the burn fee for each. Because fees burn rather than fund any operator, a sybil army cost grows linearly while its voting power stays fixed at one-vote-per-agent.
